query: Protocol for generation and culture of human trophoblast organoids
title: Establishment and differentiation of long-term trophoblast organoid cultures from the human placenta
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for generation and culture of human trophoblast organoids

### Overview

This protocol details the generation, culture, maintenance, passaging, and single-cell isolation of human trophoblast organoids from placental tissue. The process involves enzymatic digestion of villous tissue, establishment of organoid cultures in Matrigel using TOM medium, regular maintenance, and optional differentiation into extravillous trophoblasts (EVT) or isolation of single cells for analysis.

### Materials/Reagents

HAMS/F12 wash medium with penicillin/streptomycin; 20% FBS/wash medium; Wash buffer (Glucose, NaCl, KCl, phosphates, trypsin, EDTA); Collagenase V in Hams F12/10% FBS (1.0 mg/mL); Collagenase V in Advanced DMEM/10% FBS (0.5 mg/mL); Matrigel; TOM medium (two variants: Y-27632 at 2 µM and 5 µM); EVT medium components (Advanced DMEM/F12, L-glutamine, 2-mercaptoethanol, penicillin/streptomycin, BSA, ITS-X, NRG1/A83-01/Knockout serum replacement); 20% DMSO in TOM; 40% FBS in TOM; Recovery medium (Advanced DMEM/F12, N2, B27 minus vitamin A, 1% FBS, Y-27632 5 µM); 1% FBS in PBS (fresh and stored); Cell Recovery Solution; Stem Pro Accutase; Low-retention pipette tips.

### Equipment

Magnetic stirrer (Stuart, cat. no. US152); Water bath; Petri dishes; Forceps; Scalpel; 75 mL bottles with magnetic stir bars; Sterile muslin gauze and funnel; Centrifuge; Corning 48-well tissue culture plates; Humidified CO2 incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2); 1-mL pipette tips; Mettler Toledo BioClean pipette tips (cat. no. RT-200FLR) or similar small-bore tips; Electronic pipettor with 'mix' function; 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes; 5-mL polypropylene test tubes; Falcon test tubes with cell strainer snap caps (35-µm nylon mesh); ibidi dish; Four-well plate.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain sterile conditions throughout all procedures. Use low-retention pipette tips to prevent loss of organoids due to sticking. Always wash pipette tips in 1% FBS/PBS before use. Keep Matrigel on ice to prevent solidification and avoid forming air bubbles during resuspension. Avoid excessive force when breaking up organoids to maintain viability. Do not over-digest tissue to preserve cell viability and minimize stromal contamination. Monitor cultures carefully for spheroids derived from decidual glands, which indicate contamination.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-experiment Setup

1. Prepare wash medium by supplementing HAMS/F12 medium with 1× penicillin/streptomycin (100 units of penicillin and 0.1 mg/mL streptomycin). Store the medium at 4 °C for up to 1 month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare 20% (vol/vol) FBS/wash medium fresh immediately before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare wash buffer by dissolving 0.3 g Glucose, 12 g NaCl, 0.3 g KCl, 1.725 g disodium hydrogen orthophosphate, 0.3 g potassium dihydrogen orthophosphate, 2 g trypsin, and 0.2 g EDTA in 1 L of water. Filter, sterilize, aliquot, and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare 1.0 mg/mL Collagenase V solution in Hams F12 supplemented with 10% (vol/vol) FBS fresh immediately before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare 0.5 mg/mL Collagenase V solution in Advanced DMEM supplemented with 10% (vol/vol) FBS fresh immediately before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Thaw Matrigel on ice overnight at 4 °C. Mix thoroughly, aliquot into desired quantities in Eppendorf tubes, and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. Avoid freeze/thaw cycles. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare TOM medium containing Advanced DMEM/F12, N2 supplement (manufacturer's recommended concentration), B27 supplement minus vitamin A (manufacturer's recommended concentration), Primocin 100 μg/mL, N-Acetyl-L-cysteine 1.25 mM, L-glutamine 2 mM, recombinant human EGF 50 ng/mL, CHIR99021 1.5 µM, recombinant human R-spondin-1 80 ng/mL, recombinant human FGF-2 100 ng/mL, recombinant human HGF 50 ng/mL, A83-01 500 nM, prostaglandin E2 2.5 µM, and Y-27632 2 µM. Store at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Prepare TOM medium containing Advanced DMEM/F12, N2 supplement (manufacturer's recommended concentration), B27 supplement minus vitamin A (manufacturer's recommended concentration), Primocin 100 μg/mL, N-Acetyl-L-cysteine 1.25 mM, L-glutamine 2 mM, recombinant human EGF 50 ng/mL, CHIR99021 1.5 µM, recombinant human R-spondin-1 80 ng/mL, recombinant human FGF-2 100 ng/mL, recombinant human HGF 50 ng/mL, A83-01 500 nM, prostaglandin E2 2.5 µM, and Y-27632 5 µM. Store at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Prepare medium containing Advanced DMEM/F12, L-glutamine 2 mM, 2-mercaptoethanol 0.1 mM, penicillin/streptomycin solution 0.5% (vol/vol), BSA 0.3% (vol/vol), ITS-X supplement 1% (vol/vol), NRG1 100 ng/mL, A83-01 7.5 µM, and Knockout serum replacement 4% (vol/vol). Store at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
10. Prepare EVT medium (cat. no. 1 without NRG1) containing Advanced DMEM/F12, L-glutamine 2 mM, 2-mercaptoethanol 0.1 mM, penicillin/streptomycin solution 0.5% (vol/vol), BSA 0.3% (vol/vol), ITS-X supplement 1% (vol/vol), A83-01 7.5 µM, and Knockout serum replacement 4% (vol/vol). Store at 4°C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->
11. Prepare 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in TOM fresh immediately before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S11 -->
12. Prepare 40% (vol/vol) FBS in TOM fresh immediately before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S12 -->
13. Prepare recovery medium containing Advanced DMEM/F12, N2 supplement, B27 supplement minus vitamin A, 1% (vol/vol) FBS, and Y-27632 5 µM. Store at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S13 -->
14. Prepare 1% (vol/vol) FBS in PBS. Keep cold and make fresh immediately before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S14 -->
15. Prepare 1% (vol/vol) FBS in PBS. Keep cold and store at 4 °C for up to 1 month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S15 -->

## Enzymatic Digestion of Placental Tissue

### 1.5−2 h

1. Transfer placental samples into wash medium at room temperature (RT, 21−24 °C) and process within one hour. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Pre-warm 0.2% trypsin-250/0.02% EDTA/PBS to 37 °C in a water bath. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Wash the placental tissue in wash medium on a magnetic stirrer at RT with gentle stirring for >10 min to remove contaminating blood and other maternal uterine cells as much as possible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Wash placental tissue thoroughly but gently to avoid damage of villi. Speed setting between 1−2 is considered gentle when using the magnetic stirrer (Stuart, cat. no. US152). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: When starting from surgically removed placental samples, ensure that decidual tissue is not present as this will aggravate organoid contamination. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
4. Tip the placental sample in its wash medium into a petri dish and transfer the tissue with forceps into a clean dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
5. Remove any visible blood clots with forceps taking care not to damage the villi. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
6. Hold down one end of the placenta and scrape villi from the chorionic membrane with a scalpel. Discard the remaining fetal membrane. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
7. Transfer scraped villi into 75 mL pre-warmed 0.2% trypsin-250/0.02% EDTA in a bottle with a magnetic stir bar. Seal the lid and place on a heated magnetic stirrer at 37 °C with gentle stirring to digest for 3-5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Stir gently to avoid decrease in viability of cells. Speed setting between 1−2 is considered gentle when using the magnetic stirrer (Stuart, cat. no. US152). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
8. Filter the disaggregated cell suspension through a sterile muslin gauze placed in a funnel, and wash through immediately with digestion stop solution (wash medium supplemented with 20% FBS) to arrest trypsin digestion. Retain the gauze with partially digested remnants. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
9. Centrifuge at 400g for 5 mins at RT to pellet the filtrate and resuspend the cell pellet in wash medium until Step 12 (this is ‘tissue digest 1'). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
10. Retrieve undigested tissue from the gauze and digest further with 12 mL collagenase V solution 1.0 mg/mL in Hams F12/10% FBS in a bottle with a magnetic stir bar. Seal the lid and place on a heated magnetic stirrer at 37 °C with gentle stirring for 3-5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not over digest the tissue as this will result in more placental stromal cells in the digest and decreased viability of cells. Cell viability is expected to be 88.4% after this step (as determined by live/dead stain after flow cytometric analysis). (The viability of 88.4% is based on the following results seen when assessing cells from 3 different placentas: 96.1%, 86.1%, 83.0%). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Speed setting between 1−2 is considered gentle when using the magnetic stirrer (Stuart, cat. no. US152). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S15 -->
11. Filter the resultant cell suspension as described in Step 8 and centrifuge to pellet cells as described in Step 9 (this is ‘tissue digest 2'). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S16 -->
12. Pool the cells obtained in Steps 9 (tissue digest 1) and 11 (tissue digest 2) and wash in Advanced DMEM/F12 medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S17 -->

## Initiation and Establishment of Trophoblast Organoid Cultures

### Day 0

1. Resuspend pellet from step 12 in 1 mL Advanced DMEM/F12 medium, transfer to a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT to pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Remove the supernatant and estimate the volume of the pellet. Flick the tube to loosen the pellet and place on ice for 2−3 min. Add 10× volume:volume of ice-cold Matrigel and pipette gently to mix. Place tube immediately back onto ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Matrigel should be thawed completely before use and should always be kept on ice to avoid it solidifying. Take care not to form air bubbles during resuspension of cell pellet with Matrigel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Remove as much supernatant as possible before resuspending in Matrigel to avoid diluting it. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: The 10× volume:volume ratio is important for successful trophoblast organoid derivation. If the placental digest is too diluted, the trophoblast organoids form and grow slowly. Additionally, having too few organoids in each droplet makes it challenging to passage and propagate. Alternatively, if the placental digest is too concentrated it is hard to visualize gland contamination. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
3. Pipette a 25-μL drop of Matrigel/cell suspension into the center of each well of a Corning 48-well tissue culture plate. Place in the incubator to set for at least 15 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
4. Overlay each drop with 250 μL TOM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
5. Place cultures in 5% CO2 in a humidified incubator at 37 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->

### Days 1-7

1. Replace medium every 2−3 d. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S01 -->

### ~7-10 d

1. Examine cultures for the appearance of small and dense organoid clusters. These are usually visible by ~7-10 d. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Monitor the cultures carefully for the presence of spheroids. Due to the close contact of the placenta to the decidua, even upon separation of the two tissues, maternal cells can be present in the placental digests. Spheroids derive from decidual glands. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S02 -->

## Maintenance and Passaging of Trophoblast Organoid Cultures

### 1.5 h

1. Monitor the appearance of the organoids regularly, and when at least 50% of organoids reach a diameter of 200-300 µm (usually between 7-10 d following Step 19 after derivation or Step 32 of established cultures) proceed to the following steps to passage the cultures. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not wait too long to passage the organoids. The larger they are, the more difficult they are to break up, with fewer proliferative cells present. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not passage the wells if spheroids are present. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
2. Without removing the culture medium, using a 1-mL pipette tip scrape backward and forward across the growth surface of each well to detach the Matrigel drop into the medium. Aspirate the medium together with the detached Matrigel droplet and transfer the contents of the well into 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes at a ratio of at maximum four wells per tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
3. Add another ~300 µL of wash medium to the well to collect any remaining organoids. Add this to the Eppendorf. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
4. Centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT to pellet. Remove the supernatant and add ~150 μL Advanced DMEM/F12 to each tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
5. Pipette up and down ~400 times through a small-bore pipette tip (we use a Mettler Toledo, BioClean, cat. no. RT-200FLR) to break up the organoids and the Matrigel. We recommend using an electronic pipettor with a ‘mix' function and its uptake volume set to 150 µL for this step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S07 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Avoid formation of bubbles. This makes it difficult to break up the organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S08 -->
6. Add 1 mL Advanced DMEM/F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT. Remove supernatant. Add 500 μL of pre-warmed (37 °C) Stem Pro Accutase and place in a humidified incubator at 37 °C for 5−6 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not exceed recommended digestion time. This will result in low viability of cells. Increased digestion times will result in increased cellular debris and lysed cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S10 -->
7. Add 1 mL Advanced DMEM/F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT. Remove supernatant. Add 150 μL Advanced DMEM/F12 and pipette up and down manually a further ~80 times using moderate force. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S11 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not use excessive force. Organoids need to be broken up properly otherwise they will not propagate and expand. Replating organoids that have not been broken up will just make them increase in size, become dark and more difficult to passage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S12 -->
8. Add 1 mL Advanced DMEM/F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT. Remove supernatant. The pellet at this stage should contain very little Matrigel, which, if present can be seen as an opaque ring just above the pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S13 -->
9. Flick the tubes to resuspend the pellets. Place tubes on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S14 -->
10. Working one tube at a time, add ice-cold Matrigel, mix gently and replace the tube on ice. Allow 25 µL Matrigel per well to be plated, remembering to subtract the estimated volume of any residual Matrigel which remains in the pellet. Pool organoids together and mix gently to distribute them evenly throughout the Matrigel. Organoids growing optimally can be passaged at 1:2 every 7-10 d. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S15 -->
11. Dispense 25-µL drops carefully onto the center of the growth area of wells of a 48-well culture plate, taking care not to create bubbles. Keep tubes on ice while pipetting the droplets. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S16 -->
12. Place culture plate in the incubator for at least 15 min to allow Matrigel to set. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S17 -->
13. Add 250 µL TOM to each well and continue to incubate organoids. After 7-10 d, expand the cultures for experiments (by repeating Steps 20-32) or proceed to the next stage to differentiate the organoids and thereby generate EVT (Steps 33-38) or proceed to the single-cell isolation procedure (Step 39A to isolate cells for single-cell analyses or in preparation for clonal expansion). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S18 -->

## Single-Cell Isolation

### 3 h

1. If you are starting with organoids from Step 32, proceed to option A. If you are starting with organoids from the previous step, proceed to option B. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S01 -->

### 1.2 h

#### Branch A: Single-cell isolation from villous trophoblast organoids

1. (i) Without removing the culture medium, using a 1-mL pipette tip, scrape backward and forward across the growth surface of each well to detach the Matrigel drop into the medium. Transfer the contents of the wells into 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes at a ratio of three or four wells per tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S01 -->
2. (ii) Centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT to pellet. Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of Cell Recovery Solution. Place the tube horizontally on ice to avoid organoids pelleting. Place on ice for 1 h. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S02 -->

#### Branch B: Single-cell isolation from extravillous trophoblast organoids

1. (i) Remove the culture medium from the ibidi dish. Wash the dish with PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T2-S01 -->
2. (ii) Add 1.5 mL of Cell Recovery Solution directly to the dish. Place the entire dish on ice and make sure that all of the Matrigel droplets are submerged in the solution. Keep on ice for 1 h. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T2-S02 -->
3. (iii) Collect solution and transfer into 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes. Pipette up and down to rinse the dish with the solution. This will dislodge any cells still adhered to the bottom of the dish. Gently scrape the dish while dispensing the solution to remove cells if many are still adhered. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T2-S03 -->

### Post-Isolation Processing

1. Centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT to pellet. Remove the supernatant and wash the pellet in ice-cold PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Always wash pipette tips in 1% FBS/PBS to avoid loss of organoids due to sticking. Use low-retention tips during all steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S02 -->
2. Centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT to pellet. Remove the supernatant and add 200 µL of wash medium for single-cell isolation. Pipette up and down ~400 times through a small-bore pipette tip to break up the organoids. We recommend using an electronic pipettor with a ‘mix' function and its uptake volume set to 150 µL for this step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S03 -->
3. Add 1 mL Advanced DMEM/F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT. Remove supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S04 -->
4. Add 500 µL of pre-warmed (37 °C) Stem Pro Accutase and transfer to a four-well plate. Place in a humidified incubator at 37 °C for 5 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S05 -->
5. Transfer cell suspension to a 5-mL polypropylene test tube and add 1 mL of wash medium. Centrifuge at 600g for 6 min at RT to pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S06 -->
6. Remove the supernatant and resuspend in pre-warmed (37 °C) 500 µL of 0.5 mg/mL Collagenase V solution. Transfer cell suspension into a four-well dish and place in a humidified incubator at 37 °C for 15 min. Disrupt/shake suspension halfway through incubation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S07 -->
7. Transfer cell suspension back into the same 5-mL polypropylene test tube and dilute suspension in 2 mL of wash medium. Allow cells to settle for 1 min (large clumps will pellet) and remove the top 2 mL of the solution and filter through a Falcon test tube with cell strainer snap cap (cells that pass through the filter correspond to ‘organoids digest 1'). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S08 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: The cell strainer has a 35-µm nylon mesh filter to remove cell clumps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S09 -->
8. Resuspend the remaining solution containing large clumps of cells in pre-warmed (37 °C) 500 μL of 0.5 m/mL Collagenase V solution and place in the incubator for another 15 min (to start the process of collecting ‘organoid digest 2'). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S10 -->
9. Centrifuge the cells obtained in Step 46 (organoids digest 1) at 600g for 6 min to pellet (supernatant can be discarded) and then resuspend in wash medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S11 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Keep filtered cells on ice to avoid cells re-aggregating. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S12 -->
10. Collect the cells obtained in Step 47 (‘organoids digest 2'), dilute in wash medium and filter through a Falcon test tube with cell strainer snap cap. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S13 -->
11. Centrifuge the cells that pass through the filter in step 49 at 600g for 6 min at RT to pellet cells (discard supernatant) and resuspend in wash medium (organoids digest 2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S14 -->
12. Pool cell suspensions from Steps 48 (organoid digest 1) and 50 (organoids digest 2) into one tube. Centrifuge the combined suspension at 600g for 6 min at RT and resuspend in 1 mL total of wash media to determine total cell number in suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S15 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Keep cell suspension on ice to avoid cells re-aggregating. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S16 -->
